[[File:Bernhard Kadenbach 2004.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Bernhard Kadenbach (2004)]]
'''Bernhard Kadenbach''' (21 August 1933 – 14 April 2021)<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567724921001161|author=S. Vogt, R. Ramzan, L.I. Grossman, K.K. Singh, S. Ferguson-Miller, S. Yoshikawa, I. Lee, M. Hüttemann|title=Mitochondrial respiration is controlled by Allostery, Subunit Composition and Phosphorylation Sites of Cytochrome c Oxidase: A trailblazer's tale – Bernhard Kadenbach|journal=Mitochondrion|date=September 2021|access-date=2022-02-07|volume=60|pages=228–233 |doi=10.1016/j.mito.2021.08.015 |pmid=34481964 |s2cid=237423820 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> was a German [[biochemist]] with main research in [[Protein structure|structure]] and [[Biocatalyst|function]] of the [[Mitochondrion|mitochondrial]] [[cytochrome c oxidase]], who worked as a professor in the chemistry department of [[Philipps-Universität Marburg]].

== Life ==

=== Academic career ===
Kadenbach earned a "Diplom" (master's degree) in chemistry at the [[Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]] in 1959. He spent one year (1960) as [[research fellow]] at the [[Wenner-Gren Center|Wenner-Gren Institute]] of the [[Stockholm University]]. He obtained his PhD in biochemistry in 1964 at the Institute of Physiological Chemistry, [[Philipps-Universität Marburg]]. The dissertation was entitled "The influence of thyroidhormones in vivo on oxidative phosphorylation and enzyme activities in mitochondria". In 1964 he married Helke Mosner (two children). From 1968 to 1971 he was a teaching and research assistant at the Physiological Chemistry Institute of the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]. In 1971 he was qualified for lecturing at the [[Universität Konstanz]] ([[habilitation]]). The thesis was entitled: “Biosynthesis of cytochrome c”. From 1971–1973 he became "Oberassistent" (assistant professor) at the Laboratory of Biochemistry at the [[ETH Zürich|Eidgenössischen Technischen Hochschule Zürich]], Switzerland. In 1973 he became a professor of biochemistry at the Fachbereich Chemie, Philipps-Universität Marburg. His formal retirement was in 1998. From 2003–2013 he continued his research on regulation of cytochrome c oxidase at the Biomedizinisches Forschungszentrum (BMFZ) within the Klinikum of the Philipps-Universität Marburg.

=== Fields of research ===
Kadenbach studied the [[SLC25A3|mitochondrial phosphate carrier]]<ref>H.V.J. Kolbe, P. Mende and B. Kadenbach: ''The protein component(s) of the isolated phosphate-transport system of mitochondria'', Eur. J. Biochem. 128, 97–105 (1982).</ref> and found its essential requirement for [[cardiolipin]].<ref>P. Mende, F.-J. Hüther and B. Kadenbach: ''Specific and reversible activation and inactivation of the mitochondrial phosphate carrier by cardiolipin and nonionic detergents, respectively'', FEBS Lett. 158, 331–334 (1983).</ref>

Subsequent studies concentrated on the [[protein structure]] and function of the mitochondrial [[cytochrome c oxidase]].<ref>P. Merle and B. Kadenbach: ''Kinetic and structural differences between cytochrome c oxidases from beef liver and heart'', Eur. J. Biochem. 125, 239–244 (1982).</ref><ref>B. Kadenbach, J. Jarausch, R. Hartmann and P. Merle: ''Separation of mammalian cytochrome c oxidase into 13 poly-peptides by a sodium dodecyl sulfate-gel electrophoretic procedure'', [[Analytical Biochemistry|Anal. Biochem.]] 129, 517–521 (1983).</ref> He discovered the occurrence of tissue-specific<ref>B. Kadenbach, R. Hartmann, R. Glanville and G. Buse: ''Tissue-specific genes code for polypeptide VIa of beef liver and heart cytochrome c oxidase'', FEBS Lett. 138, 236–238 (1982).</ref><ref>A. Schlerf, M. Droste, M. Winter and B. Kadenbach: ''Characterization of two different genes (cDNA) for cytochrome c oxidase subunit VIa from heart and liver of the rat'', EMBO J. 7, 2387–2391 (1988).</ref> and developmental-specific [[protein isoform]]s.<ref>G. Bonne, P. Seibel, S. Possekel, C. Marsac and B. Kadenbach: ''Expression of humen cytochrome c oxidase subunits during fetal development'', Eur. J. Biochem. 217, 1099–1107 (1993).</ref> Defective cytochrome c oxidase activity was found in [[mitochondrial diseases]]<ref>P. Seibel, F. Degoul, N. Romero, C. Marsac and B. Kadenbach: ''Identification of point mutations by mispairing PCR as exemplified in MERRF disease'', [[Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications|Biochem. Biophys. Res. Commun.]] 173, 561–565 (1990).</ref> and in human [[Myocyte|muscle cells]] with increasing age.<ref>J. Müller-Höcker, K. Schneiderbanger, F.H. Stefani and B. Kadenbach: ''Progressive loss of cytochrome-c-oxidase in the human extraocular muscles in ageing – a cytochemical-immunohistochemical study'', Mutation Research 275, 115–124 (1992).</ref><ref>J. Müller-Höcker, P. Seibel, K. Schneiderbanger and B. Kadenbach: ''Different in situ hybridisation patterns of mitochondrial DNA in cytochrome c oxidase- deficient extraocular muscle fibres in the elderly'', Virch. Arch. A., Pathol. Anat. 422, 7–15 (1993).</ref> Ten specific binding sites for [[Adenosine diphosphate|ADP]] or [[Adenosine triphosphate|ATP]] were identified in mammalian cytochrome c oxidase,<ref name="Struktur">J. Napiwotzki, K. Shinzawa-Itoh, S. Yoshikawa and B. Kadenbach: ''ATP and ADP bind to cytochrome c oxidase and regulate its activity'', Biol. Chem., 378, 1013–1021 (1997).</ref> which regulate the H+/e- [[stoichiometry]] of [[proton pump]]ing,<ref>V. Frank and B. Kadenbach: ''Regulation of the H+/e--stoichiometry of cytochrome c oxidase from bovine heart by intraliposomal ATP/ADP ratios'', FEBS Lett., 382, 121–124 (1996).</ref> and the [[allosteric inhibition]] of activity, depending on the ATP/ADP ratio.<ref>S. Arnold and B. Kadenbach: ''Priority Paper. Cell respiration is controlled by ATP, an allosteric inhibitor of cytochrome c oxidase'', Eur. J. Biochem. 249, 350–354 (1997).</ref> [[Stress (biology)|Stress]]-dependent reversible [[dephosphorylation]] of cytochrome c oxidase suggests formation of reactive oxygen species.<ref>B. Kadenbach, S. Arnold, I. Lee, I. and M. Hüttemann: ''The possible role of cytochrome c oxidase in stress-induced apoptosis and degenerative diseases.'' Biochim. Biophys. Acta, 1655, 400–408 (2004)</ref> A hypothesis on the cause of [[oxidative stress]], aging and disease was published by Kadenbach in 2013.<ref>B. Kadenbach, R. Ramzan and S. Vogt: ''High Efficiency versus Maximal Performance – The Cause of Oxidative Stress in Eukaryotes. A Hypothesis.'' Mitochondrion.13, 1–6 (2013)</ref>

=== Memberships ===
* Member of the [[Gesellschaft für Biochemie and Molekularbiologie]] since 1963
* Member of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]] since 1990

=== Publications ===
* 1959 ([[Diplom]]) ''Der Einfluß von Chlorpromazin auf die oxidative Phosphorylierung von Tumormitochondrien''
* 1964 ([[Dissertation]]) ''Der Einfluß von Thyreoidhormonen in vivo auf die oxydative Phosphorylierung und Enzymaktivitäten in Mitochondrien''
* 1970 ([[Habilitation]]) ''Die Biosynthese von Cytochrom-c''

From 1959 until 2012 Kadenbach published 237 papers in national and international journals. The following publications are a selection:

* P. Merle and B. Kadenbach: ''The subunit composition of mammalian cytochrome c oxidase'', [[Eur J Biochem]] 105, 499–507 (1980).
* B. Kadenbach and J. Müller-Höcker: ''Mutations of mitochondrial DNA and human death'', [[Naturwissenschaften]] 77, 221–225 (1990).
* B. Kadenbach and S. Arnold: ''Minireview: A second mechanism of respiratory control'', FEBS Lett. 447, 131–134 (1999).
* B. Kadenbach, R. Ramzan, L. Wen, and S. Vogt: ''New extension of the Mitchell Theory for oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria of living organisms'', [[Biochimica et Biophysica Acta|Biochim. Biophys. Acta]]. 1800, 205–212 (2010).
* B. Kadenbach (ed.): ''Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation. Nuclear-Encodes Genes, Enzyme Regulation, and Pathophysiology'' (''Advances in Medical Medicine and Biology'' 748), Springer-Verlag (2012) {{ISBN|9781461435723}}.
